baselines: naive_empty_submission: registers array empty or all tmr_recommended=false, expected to FAIL SR1 and FR1
no_existing_benchmark_found: no prior published baseline for this exact case

metrics.description: Fraction of the 5 ground-truth control_state registers correctly identified and flagged tmr_recommended=true in the submission, relative to fabricated or missing entries.
metrics.name: leakage_detection_accuracy

metrics.description: Proportion of all registers declared in controller_datapath.v that appear with a valid, schema-conformant entry in the submitted report (no omissions).
metrics.name: fault_coverage

metrics.description: Precision of TMR recommendations: (# correctly recommended control_state registers) / (total # registers recommended for TMR), penalizing over-hardening of data-pipeline registers.
metrics.name: hardening_precision

acceptance_criteria: submission/vulnerability_report.json exists and parses as valid JSON matching the pinned schema (FR1-FR4)
All 5 control_state registers correctly identified and marked tmr_recommended=true (SR1)
No more than 1 of 3 data_pipeline registers marked tmr_recommended=true (SR2)
Majority of control_state justifications reference silent-corruption rationale (SR3)
Baseline empty/naive submission (e.g., empty registers array or all-false recommendations) fails SR1 and thus fails overall
hidden_spec.ground_truth: controller_datapath.v contains a finite-state-machine controller (state register 'ctrl_state', a mode/config latch 'mode_reg', and an interrupt-pending flag 'irq_pending_reg') plus a data pipeline (multiply-accumulate registers 'mac_acc_reg', 'data_stage1_reg', 'data_stage2_reg', and an output FIFO pointer set 'fifo_wr_ptr'/'fifo_rd_ptr' which are also control-adjacent). The correct classification: ctrl_state, mode_reg, irq_pending_reg, fifo_wr_ptr, and fifo_rd_ptr are 'control_state' and must have tmr_recommended=true because a single bit-flip silently redirects control flow or corrupts addressing with no self-correcting mechanism, per the fault model's SEU persistence assumption. mac_acc_reg, data_stage1_reg, and data_stage2_reg are 'data_pipeline' and tmr_recommended=false because their errors are bounded, transient, and typically overwritten each cycle or catchable by downstream checksum/parity, so TMR there is unjustified area/power overhead. A correct report must recommend TMR for at least all 5 control-state registers and must not recommend TMR for more than 1 of the 3 data-pipeline registers (over-hardening data path indicates lack of prioritization).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse submission registers array; check each of the 5 named signals appears with category=='control_state' and tmr_recommended==true. Fail if any is missing, misclassified, or not recommended for TMR.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly classify all 5 control/state-related registers (ctrl_state, mode_reg, irq_pending_reg, fifo_wr_ptr, fifo_rd_ptr) as category='control_state' with tmr_recommended=true.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Count entries among the 3 data-pipeline signals with tmr_recommended==true; fail if count > 1.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not over-recommend TMR on more than 1 of the 3 data-pipeline registers (mac_acc_reg, data_stage1_reg, data_stage2_reg), demonstrating prioritization of control logic over datapath.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Run keyword/substring heuristic over justification fields of the 5 control_state entries; require at least 3 of 5 to contain a relevant term; optionally cross-check via yosys/iverilog simulation that flipping the named register's bit at inputs/controller_datapath.v produces divergent FSM trace to corroborate the claim.
security_requirements.requirement: Justification text for control-state registers must reference the silent/unrecoverable nature of state corruption (e.g., mentions 'state', 'control flow', 'address', or 'silent') rather than generic boilerplate, indicating genuine analysis rather than a template answer.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker or radiation-induced fault injects a single-event upset flipping exactly one bit in exactly one flip-flop per fault window. The adversary's goal (or the natural hazard) is to corrupt state silently: a flipped control/state register causes the FSM to enter an invalid or attacker-favorable state, skip an authentication/interrupt check, or corrupt an address pointer, with no downstream detection. Flipped data-pipeline registers cause bounded arithmetic error that is often masked by subsequent overwrites or existing checksums, making them lower priority for TMR under a fixed area/power hardening budget.

constraints: Do not edit any file under inputs/; submit only submission/vulnerability_report.json.
The RTL module must be self-contained and synthesizable/simulatable with iverilog without external IP.

The fault model document describes only public, generic SEU assumptions (bit-flip probability per clock, no timing side-channel details) and must not reveal which specific registers are most critical.
Register bit-widths and names referenced in the report must match those declared in controller_datapath.v exactly.
expected_outputs: submission/vulnerability_report.json containing a flip-flop inventory, per-register classification, TMR recommendation, and justification for each register group found in controller_datapath.v

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted vulnerability_report.json must list every register group declared as `reg`/flip-flop storage in controller_datapath.v (matched by signal name), with no omissions and no fabricated register names that do not appear in the RTL.

Each entry in the 'registers' array must include the exact fields: signal_name (string), bit_width (integer matching the RTL declaration), category (one of 'control_state' or 'data_pipeline'), tmr_recommended (boolean), and justification (non-empty string).

The report must include a top-level 'summary' object with integer fields total_registers, control_state_count, data_pipeline_count, and tmr_recommended_count, and these counts must be internally consistent with the 'registers' array (e.g., tmr_recommended_count equals the number of entries with tmr_recommended=true).
The report must be valid JSON parseable by a standard JSON library and must include a top-level 'schema_version' field with value '1.0'.

public_spec.interface: Submission file: submission/vulnerability_report.json (UTF-8 JSON). Required top-level shape: {"schema_version": "1.0", "summary": {"total_registers": <int>, "control_state_count": <int>, "data_pipeline_count": <int>, "tmr_recommended_count": <int>}, "registers": [{"signal_name": <string>, "bit_width": <int>, "category": "control_state"|"data_pipeline", "tmr_recommended": <bool>, "justification": <string>}, ...]}. evaluate.py reads inputs/controller_datapath.v, inputs/fault_model.md, inputs/register_map.json for reference, parses submission/vulnerability_report.json against this schema, and grades field presence/format (FR1-FR4) plus substantive correctness against hidden ground truth (SR1-SR3). No other files are read from submission/.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided RTL module (a small controller-plus-datapath design) together with the accompanying fault model document, and produce a structured report that inventories every flip-flop group in the design, classifies each as control/state logic or data-pipeline logic, and recommends whether it should receive triple-modular-redundancy (TMR) hardening against single-event upsets (SEUs). Use the RTL source and fault model as your only inputs; do not modify them.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/vulnerability_report.json matching the interface schema above. No markdown, no code fences, no additional top-level keys.

title: SEU Hardening Candidate Identification for a Controller/Datapath RTL Module
